text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Prod serving cluster 'prod-gpu-12' is reporting repeated OOMs during prefill. Containers restarting. Paging oncall.

sarah: seeing a spike in long-context requests from a single customer, TTLs ~200s. Containers restart after prefill step.

oncall-ryan: I'm on it. grabbing logs now, switching my pager to high. @devops-lee can you confirm if autoscaler kicked in?

devops-lee: autoscaler did not trigger; node pool at capacity. I see 6/8 GPUs with fragmented KV caches. Eviction logs show repeated prefill allocations.

nina: rolling up short triage: likely long prompt prefill causing sustained VRAM growth -> OOM -> container restart. Impact: approx 12% error rate for requests to route model-x-heavy in us-west-2.

matt: customer-ops, any reported customer disruptions yet?

customer-ops: one customer reported degraded completions, downstream retries increased. no SLA breach reported yet, but increased error tail.

oncall-ryan: paste of recent container log (truncated):
```
2025-06-02T03:44:12Z WARN prefill: incoming request len=120k tokens
2025-06-02T03:44:13Z INFO kvcache: allocating 22GB for prefix
E2025-06-02T03:44:14Z cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED on device 0
E2025-06-02T03:44:14Z runtime: GPU OOM during prefill; killing container pid=1423
2025-06-02T03:44:15Z container: restart attempt 1
```

sarah: that CUBLAS alloc fail matches OOM. We should enable the cold-model fallback for route model-x-heavy and reduce per-request batch size via routing policy.

devops-lee: I can flip cold fallback and add a temporary routing policy to cap window to 32k tokens for new requests. Doing it now.

infra-bot: automated action applied: routing policy updated for model-x-heavy: max_prefill_tokens=32000, fallback_variant=coldmodel-v2. ChangeID=chg-20250602-01

nina: good. also enable aggressive KV eviction on affected nodes: set kvcache.max_prefill_cache=6GB.

devops-lee: applied kvcache change on pool prod-gpu-12. will monitor.

oncall-ryan: monitoring metrics: prefill OOMs dropped from ~8/min to 0.8/min after changes. Latency increased for fallback requests (~120ms extra) but error rate improved.

customer-ops: drafting outbound note to the impacted customer: explain degraded completions and mitigation steps, offer post-incident review. ping me for approval.

matt: +1 on customer comms. tag legal if they want specifics.

sarah: next actions: 1) keep fallback live for 2 hours, 2) run a canary of model-x-heavy with stricter per-request validation to reject absurdly long prompts, 3) follow up with model team about prefix memory accounting.

oncall-ryan: handing off to night oncall @nina. I will set a reminder to re-evaluate in 90m. Paging handoff notes attached.

nina: taking handoff. I'll keep watch for node flaps and schedule a maintenance window if we see recurrence. thx all.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. customer impact reduced. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1749999999

sarah: final note: root cause likely unbounded prefill allocations for very long prompts + fragmented KVcache under high concurrency. plan: server-side prefill limits + metric alert for prefill allocation per-request. I'll start a ticket.

customer-ops: customer note sent (internal copy). will coordinate follow-up postmortem timeline if needed.

matt: nice fast mitigation. retiring pager. :thumbsup:
